Not one of them starts with a DEX header, so there is no code in this artifact that Android could run. Whatever executes is produced at runtime. This is what a packer looks like, and every other finding here describes the loader rather than the app.
%1$d of %2$d .dex entries are not DEX files.

Android will not load those directly, so they are payloads decrypted at runtime by the ones that it will. The code that runs is not in this file. This is what a packer looks like, and every other finding here describes the loader rather than the app.

The header is real and nearly empty. A build this size normally declares hundreds of thousands of methods, so the bulk of the file is data sitting behind a valid header, unpacked at runtime. This is what a packer looks like, and every other finding here describes the loader rather than the app.
If this is your build, check what your shrinker or protection tool is producing. If it is not, treat every other finding here as describing a stub.
Debug builds are signed with a debug key, ship unminified, and are rejected by Play. Findings below describe this file, not the one you would upload.
Analyse the release artifact instead: app/build/outputs/bundle/release, or the AAB from your CI.
Play refuses new apps and updates below the floor, which rises every August. This build cannot be uploaded.
Raise targetSdk to %1$d in build.gradle.kts, then retest: each level brings behaviour changes that only appear at runtime.
An unsigned package cannot be installed or uploaded.
Build a signed artifact, or check the signing config actually applied to this variant.
Play has never served an x86 build to a phone. These are bytes in every install that no user runs.
Play has never served an x86 build to a phone. These are bytes in every install that no user runs, roughly %1$s here.
An App Bundle splits by ABI automatically and the problem disappears. For an APK, add an abiFilters block for arm64-v8a and armeabi-v7a.
Any request this app makes over http:// can be read and altered on the network the user is on.
Set android:usesCleartextTraffic to false, or add a network security config that permits only the hosts that genuinely need it.
Each one is a dialog the user can refuse, and each needs a Data Safety entry in the Play listing.
Check every one is still used. A permission left behind by a removed feature costs installs and answers in the Data Safety form.
Any app on the device can start an exported component. One of these is the launcher activity and has to be; the others are entry points into this app that you may not have meant to open.
For each, confirm android:exported is deliberate and the component validates what it receives.
App data is copied to the user\'s cloud backup and restored onto new devices, including anything cached that should not travel.
Check the backup rules exclude tokens, keys and caches, or set android:allowBackup to false.
Dangerous permissions are asked for at runtime, and can be refused.
Sharing a file:// URI with another app throws FileUriExposedException.
Background services are limited, and implicit broadcasts no longer reach manifest receivers.
A notification without a channel is not shown.
Cleartext HTTP is off unless a network security config allows it.
Foreground services need the FOREGROUND_SERVICE permission.
Scoped storage is on by default, with a temporary opt-out.
Scoped storage is enforced, and requestLegacyExternalStorage is ignored.
Other installed apps are invisible unless declared in <queries>.
Background location has to be requested separately, after foreground location.
Every component with an intent filter must set android:exported.
Every PendingIntent must say FLAG_IMMUTABLE or FLAG_MUTABLE.
Foreground services can no longer be started from the background.
Exact alarms need the SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM permission.
Posting notifications needs the POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission.
READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE gives way to READ_MEDIA_IMAGES, READ_MEDIA_VIDEO and READ_MEDIA_AUDIO.
Every foreground service must declare a type, and hold that type\'s permission.
Receivers registered in code must say whether they are exported.
Implicit intents only reach exported components.
The app draws edge to edge, behind the status and navigation bars.
On screens 600dp and wider, orientation and resizability locks are ignored.
Predictive back is on, and onBackPressed is no longer called.
The temporary opt-out from the large-screen rules is gone.
This phone uses 16 KB memory pages, and these libraries cannot load on it.
The app crashes as soon as it loads native code.
64-bit libraries are aligned for 16 KB pages.
64-bit libraries not aligned for 16 KB pages: %1$s of %2$s.
Play refuses updates targeting Android 15 or later that ship them, and they will not load on 16 KB devices. Rebuild with NDK r28 or newer, or link with -Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384.
Uncompressed libraries start on 16 KB boundaries in the APK.
Uncompressed libraries not on 16 KB boundaries: %1$s of %2$s.
Android maps these straight from the APK, so where they start has to be page aligned. AGP 8.5.1 and later align them, and so does zipalign -P 16.
Ships 32-bit native code without the 64-bit version.
Play requires 64-bit code alongside 32-bit, and phones that only run 64-bit cannot install this.
No native code for this phone\'s CPU (%1$s).
No native code, so any CPU can run it.
Has native code for this phone\'s CPU (%1$s).
Has dataExtractionRules for cloud backup and device transfer.
fullBackupContent is set to false, so full-data backup is off.
Only the older fullBackupContent rules are set.
From Android 12, device-to-device transfer follows dataExtractionRules instead. Add them, with the same exclusions.
allowBackup=false no longer stops device-to-device transfer.
At this target, Android 12 and later still copy app data to a new phone. Exclude what should not travel in dataExtractionRules.
Play App Signing needs a key valid until at least then.
This phone is newer than the app\'s target.
Android runs it in compatibility mode: the changes of newer versions stay off until the app targets them.
Signed with the Android debug certificate.
Play rejects debug-signed uploads. Debug keys use a well-known password and are not kept safe, so they are not keys to ship with.
Play rejects debuggable builds, and anyone with adb access can attach a debugger to it.
No bitmaps for this phone\'s density (%1$s).
Android scales the nearest ones, which costs a little sharpness or memory. Vector drawables avoid the question.
Has resources for this phone\'s density (%1$s).
No density-specific bitmaps, so images scale cleanly on any screen.
This phone runs API %1$s; the app needs API %2$s or later.
Installs on this phone\'s Android (API %1$s, needs %2$s).
D8 or R8 says so in the DEX itself. Debug-mode code is larger and slower, and keeps what release builds strip.
Draws edge to edge on Android 15 and later. Check nothing hides under the system bars.
Uses SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM, which is off by default on Android 14.
Setting an exact alarm without it throws. Check canScheduleExactAlarms() first, and send the user to Settings when it is false.
Nothing but the launcher is open to other apps without a permission.
Components any app can start, with no permission guarding them.
Requires hardware this phone does not have.
Play hides the app from phones like this one. Mark the feature android:required=\"false\" if the app works without it.
This phone has every hardware feature the app requires.
Declares foreground service types without FOREGROUND_SERVICE.
startForeground throws a SecurityException without it.
Foreground service types missing their permission.
On Android 14 and later, startForeground throws a SecurityException for each of these.
Every foreground service type has its permission.
Requires OpenGL ES %1$s; this phone has %2$s.
Adaptive icon, so launchers can shape and animate it.
Launchers shrink it onto a plain plate to fit their shape. Add an adaptive-icon in mipmap-anydpi-v26.
Has a monochrome layer for themed icons.
Android 13 or later is needed to read the monochrome layer.
With themed icons on, this one keeps its own colours among icons that match the wallpaper. Add a <monochrome> to the adaptive icon.
It raises the memory ceiling and hides leaks until they matter more. Use it only if the app truly needs the room.
requestLegacyExternalStorage has no effect at this target.
On Android 11 and later the app gets scoped storage regardless. Test file access there.
Android extracts them at install, so they take space twice. Stored uncompressed, they load straight from the APK.
The manifest could not be decoded, so rules set in it are unknown.
Upload it to Play Console with the release, or crash stack traces stay unreadable.
If the app notifies at all, nothing appears on Android 13 and later.
R8 ran but kept most names. Look for -dontobfuscate or broad -keep rules, which also keep code R8 could have removed.
Locked orientations are ignored on large screens at this target.
On tablets, foldables and desktop windows, these activities rotate and resize like any other. Test them there.
Large screens show them letterboxed. From targetSdk 36, Android ignores the lock on screens 600dp and wider.
WebP is usually a quarter to a third smaller at the same quality, and Android Studio converts them in one step.
Nothing here is likely to break after install.
Content providers any app can read, with no permission.
Whatever they expose is readable by every app on the device. Guard them with readPermission, or set exported to false.
Full mode, the default since AGP 8, optimises more. Remove android.enableR8.fullMode=false once the keep rules allow it.
Code is not shrunk with R8.
An unshrunk build is larger and slower, and its code reads like the source. Turn on minification for the release build.
No compiler marker in the DEX.
D8 and R8 always leave one, so this was built another way or the marker was stripped. Shrinking cannot be confirmed.
Resource shrinking and optimisation remove unused resources and shorten the rest. They run with R8 when shrinkResources is on.
Resource paths are shortened, so resources were optimised.
Declares no support for large screens.
Tablets run it in compatibility mode, or Play hides it from them. Remove the supports-screens restriction.
Installing needs about %1$s free; this phone has less.
Only adb install -t accepts it. Play rejects it, and phones refuse it from a file. Android Studio adds this when it runs the app.
No longer ships native code for some CPUs.
Phones that relied on these stop receiving updates, or fail to install this one.
Android refuses the update with INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE unless the key was rotated with APK Signature Scheme v3.
Users on older Android keep the version they have and stop getting updates.
Existing users see a dialog for each the first time the app asks. Explain why before it appears.
Android installs this as a separate app, not as an update.
Every behaviour change between the two now applies to existing users. Target SDK Checker lists them.
Android refuses a downgrade with INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE, and Play refuses the upload.
A phone reinstalls it over the old one, but Play rejects an upload that does not increase it.
Apps targeting Android 11 or later need APK Signature Scheme v2 or newer, or they fail to install.
Signed with APK Signature Scheme v2 or newer.
That is Play\'s ceiling. No later version could be uploaded.

Answer the advertising ID question under App content in Play Console.
All files access. Declare the core use in Play Console, or use MediaStore and the Storage Access Framework instead.

Reserved for alarm clock and calendar apps. Others should use SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM.
Foreground service type. Declare each type and what it is used for in Play Console.
Full-screen intents. From Android 14, only calling and alarm apps get this by default.
Health Connect data. Needs a health apps declaration.
Installing packages. Declare the core use in Play Console.
Photos and videos. Apps that use media only occasionally must use the photo picker instead.
Package visibility. Declare why the app needs to see every installed app, or use <queries>.
SMS and call log. Only the default SMS, phone or assistant app may request this.
VPN service. Needs a VpnService declaration.
